  (function () {
    var KEY = 'pstonn-theme', saved = localStorage.getItem(KEY);
    if (saved) document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', saved);
    function toggle() {
      var cur = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme');
      var sysDark = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme:dark)').matches;
      var isDark = cur ? cur === 'dark' : sysDark;
      var next = isDark ? 'light' : 'dark';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', next);
      localStorage.setItem(KEY, next);
    }
    
    
    
    
    
    document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
      if (e.target.closest && e.target.closest('[data-theme-toggle]')) toggle();
    });
    
    
    
    
    document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
      var btn = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('[data-share-pstonn]');
      if (!btn) return;
      
      
      var url = location.origin;
      var msg = 'Schedule your Stonnington visitor parking permit';
      if (navigator.share) {
        navigator.share({ title: 'p.stonn', text: msg, url: url }).catch(function () {});
      } else if (navigator.clipboard) {
        navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function () {
          btn.textContent = 'Link copied';
        }).catch(function () {});
      }
    });
  })();

<script nonce="NONCE">
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  (function () {
    var native = document.startViewTransition;
    if (!native) return;
    var noop = function () {};
    document.startViewTransition = function () {
      var t = native.apply(document, arguments);
      if (t) {
        if (t.ready && t.ready.catch) t.ready.catch(noop);
        if (t.finished && t.finished.catch) t.finished.catch(noop);
      }
      return t;
    };
  })();

  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  window.pstonnWake = (function () {
    var lock = null, want = false;
    function acquire() {
      if (!want || lock || !('wakeLock' in navigator) || document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return;
      navigator.wakeLock.request('screen').then(function (l) {
        if (!want) { try { l.release(); } catch (e) {} return; }
        lock = l;
        l.addEventListener('release', function () { lock = null; });
      }).catch(function () {}); 
    }
    function release() {
      want = false;
      if (lock) { try { lock.release(); } catch (e) {} lock = null; }
    }
    
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
      if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') acquire();
    });
    return {
      on: function () { want = true; acquire(); },
      off: release,
      
      
      
      
      sync: function () {
        var live = Array.prototype.some.call(
          document.querySelectorAll('[data-keep-awake]'),
          function (el) { return el.getClientRects().length > 0; });
        if (live) { this.on(); } else { release(); }
      }
    };
  })();
  document.addEventListener('htmx:afterSettle', function () { window.pstonnWake.sync(); });
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { window.pstonnWake.sync(); });
</script>

  addEventListener('htmx:beforeRequest', function (e) { var el = e.detail && e.detail.elt; if (el && el.classList && el.classList.contains('hx-quiet')) return; var b = document.getElementById('htmx-bar'); if (b) b.classList.add('on'); });

  addEventListener('htmx:sendError', function (e) {
    var cfg = e.detail && e.detail.requestConfig;
    if (!cfg || !cfg.boosted) return;
    if (cfg.verb === 'get' && cfg.path) { window.location.href = cfg.path; }
    else { window.location.reload(); }
  });
  
  
  
  
  
  
  addEventListener('htmx:beforeSwap', function (e) {
    var x = e.detail && e.detail.xhr;
    if (!x || x.status < 400) return;
    e.detail.shouldSwap = false;
    if (x.status === 422) {
      e.detail.isError = false;
      showToast((x.responseText || 'Something needs your attention.').trim());
      return;
    }
    var msg = 'Something went wrong. Please try again.';
    var body = x.responseText || '';
    if (body.lastIndexOf('<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><body', 0) === 0) {
      try {
        var p = new DOMParser().parseFromString(body, 'text/html').querySelector('p');
        if (p && p.textContent.trim()) msg = p.textContent.trim();
      } catch (err) {}
    }
    
    
    
    
    showToast(msg, true);
  });
  var toastTimer;
  
  function showToast(msg, sticky) {
    var t = document.getElementById('toast');
    if (!t) return;
    clearTimeout(toastTimer);
    t.textContent = msg;
    t.classList.toggle('sticky', !!sticky);
    if (sticky) {
      var x = document.createElement('button');
      x.type = 'button';
      x.className = 'toast-x';
      x.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Dismiss');
      x.textContent = '×';
      x.addEventListener('click', function () { t.classList.remove('on'); });
      t.appendChild(x);
    } else {
      toastTimer = setTimeout(function () { t.classList.remove('on'); }, 5000);
    }
    t.classList.add('on');
  }
</script>
<script nonce="NONCE">

window.popClamp = window.popClamp || function (el) {
  el.style.removeProperty('--pop-shift');
  var pad = 12, vw = document.documentElement.clientWidth;
  var r = el.getBoundingClientRect(), dx = 0;
  if (r.left < pad) dx = pad - r.left;
  else if (r.right > vw - pad) dx = vw - pad - r.right;
  if (dx) el.style.setProperty('--pop-shift', dx + 'px');
  el.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' });
};
(function () {
  if (window.appConfirm) return; 
  var pending = null;
  function dlg() { return document.getElementById('confirm-dlg'); }
  function settle(ok) {
    var d = dlg(), res = pending;
    pending = null;
    if (d && d.open) d.close();
    if (res) res(ok);
  }
  window.appConfirm = function (message, okLabel) {
    var d = dlg();
    if (!d || typeof d.showModal !== 'function') return Promise.resolve(window.confirm(message));
    if (pending) pending(false);
    d.querySelector('.dlg-msg').textContent = message;
    d.querySelector('.dlg-ok').textContent = okLabel || 'Confirm';
    d.showModal();
    return new Promise(function (res) { pending = res; });
  };
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var d = dlg();
    if (!d || !d.open) return;
    if (e.target.closest('.dlg-ok')) settle(true);
    else if (e.target.closest('.dlg-cancel') || e.target === d) settle(false); 
  });
  document.addEventListener('cancel', function (e) { 
    if (e.target === dlg() && pending) { var res = pending; pending = null; res(false); }
  }, true);
  
  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var el = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('[data-print],[data-dispatch]') : null;
    if (!el) return;
    if (el.hasAttribute('data-print')) window.print();
    var name = el.getAttribute('data-dispatch');
    
    if (name) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(name, {detail:{permit: el.getAttribute('data-dispatch-permit') || ''}}));
  });
  
  document.addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
    var f = e.target, field = f.dataset && f.dataset.plateConfirm;
    if (!field || f.__confirmed) return;
    var inp = f.querySelector('[name="' + field + '"]');
    var v = inp ? (inp.value || '').toUpperCase().replace(/[\s\-.·]+/g, '') : '';
    if (!inp || inp.offsetParent === null || !v) { delete f.dataset.confirm; return; }
    f.dataset.confirm = 'You typed ' + v + ' — check it against the car’s actual number plate. ' +
      'Letter O vs zero 0 and letter I vs one 1 are easy to mix up, and a wrong plate means the car is not covered.';
    f.dataset.confirmOk = 'It matches — continue';
  }, true);
  
  document.addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
    var f = e.target, msg = f.dataset && f.dataset.confirm;
    if (!msg) return;
    if (f.__confirmed) { f.__confirmed = false; return; }
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    appConfirm(msg, f.dataset.confirmOk).then(function (ok) {
      if (!ok) return;
      f.__confirmed = true;
      if (f.requestSubmit) f.requestSubmit(); else f.submit();
    });
  }, true);
  document.addEventListener('htmx:confirm', function (e) {
    if (!e.detail.question) return; 
    e.preventDefault();
    var elt = e.detail.elt;
    appConfirm(e.detail.question, elt && elt.dataset ? elt.dataset.confirmOk : null)
      .then(function (ok) { if (ok) e.detail.issueRequest(true); });
  });
})();

<main id="main" tabindex="-1" class="landing about">
  <section class="paper">
    <h1 class="about-h1">Security &amp; data</h1>
    <p>p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool for scheduling your City of Stonnington visitor parking permit. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the council. See <a href="/features" hx-boost="false">what p.stonn can do</a>.</p>

    <h2 class="about-h2">The short version</h2>
    <p>p.stonn signs in to your council account and changes which car is on your visitor permit, following the schedule you set. To do that it keeps a live connection to your account. That connection &mdash; and your council password, if you choose to save it &mdash; is encrypted on the server.</p>
    <p>You stay in control: disconnect any time in Settings and it takes effect immediately, and you can delete everything you&rsquo;ve stored on request. The one thing to do at your end is use a council password you don&rsquo;t use anywhere else, so nothing else of yours is exposed in the unlikely event this server is ever broken into.</p>
    <p class="sec-more">The detail is below &mdash; open any section that matters to you.</p>

    <details class="sec"><summary>What&rsquo;s encrypted, and what isn&rsquo;t</summary>
      <p>Encrypted with AES-256-GCM: your council session, its access token, your saved password, and the codes behind your printed and visitor QR links.</p>
      <p>Stored as plain text: your number plates, your schedule, your permit details, email addresses, and the activity and change logs. None of that is a login to your council account, but anyone with access to this server or its database could read it. It is kept readable because that is what running the service reliably needs.</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>How the connection ends</summary>
      <p>It lasts while the account is in use and stops after <strong>90 days with nobody signing in</strong> (anyone you share the account with counts). About a week before, p.stonn emails a one-click link to keep it going. This is deliberate: it should not hold access to the council account of someone who has moved away or stopped using it.</p>
      <p>You can also end it yourself any time &mdash; disconnect in Settings (immediate), or change your council password, which ends the stored session (an access token already issued may keep working for up to about an hour).</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>Your council password, and signing in</summary>
      <p>Saved by default, encrypted, so p.stonn can sign back in on its own when the council ends a session &mdash; without it, a lapsed session stops your schedule until you reconnect by hand. Untick &ldquo;Save my password&rdquo; when you link, or turn it off later in Settings, and it is erased and never stored again.</p>
      <p>Your p.stonn sign-in is separate: a one-time code to your verified email. You can only ever link the council account whose email matches it. (Self-hosters: the app trusts whatever verified email its sign-in layer supplies.)</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>What data p.stonn holds</summary>
      <p><strong>About you:</strong> your email, your vehicles and their plates, your schedule, your permit details, a log of the changes it made, a log of who on the account changed what, your notification settings, and the encrypted council session (plus your password, unless you turned that off).</p>
      <p><strong>About other people</strong>, only where you have used those features: the email addresses of anyone you gave shared access to or sent a guest link to, any driver email you attached to a car, and the plates visitors typed at a printed QR code. An address that bounces or reports spam goes on a do-not-email list so p.stonn stops trying it.</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>How long it is kept</summary>
      <p>Activity and change logs: 90 days. A visitor&rsquo;s plate from a printed QR: 7 days from the scan. A revoked guest link stops naming its recipient after 30 days. Sent notifications keep no message content &mdash; it is stripped the moment they go out. The server&rsquo;s own operational logs hold plates and permit IDs, plus a <strong>redacted</strong> form of email addresses (first letter and domain, not the whole address). They are size- and age-capped, so they hold about the last couple of weeks of activity rather than a permanent history. On the do-not-email list, a bounce or unsubscribe ages out after two years; a spam complaint is kept, so a request to stop never quietly expires.</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>How your data is used</summary>
      <p>Only to run this service for you. It is never sold and never used for advertising. There are no trackers or analytics &mdash; the app makes no requests to any third party from your browser. It is shared only where a feature needs it: with the email provider that delivers your notifications, the push server if you turn push on, and the council itself when it changes your permit.</p>
      <p>The server administrator can technically see what is stored on the server &mdash; that is true of any self-hosted tool. p.stonn is small and personal, and your data is used only to run the service for you: never sold, never shared beyond what a feature needs, and never looked at for anything else.</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>Deleting your data</summary>
      <p>&ldquo;Delete all my data&rdquo; in Settings clears everything from the live database straight away: your session, saved password, schedule, vehicles, guest passes, logs, and anything queued to be emailed to you. It also removes your traces from any account you were a member of, including guest passes you created there.</p>
      <p>Backups are the exception: encrypted backups run daily and thin out over time (roughly the last week daily, the last month weekly, then monthly for about three months), so deleted data can linger in a backup for up to about three months before it is gone for good. Backups are not reachable through the app and are encrypted with a key held separately from the server.</p>
    </details>

    <details class="sec"><summary>If the server were compromised</summary>
      <p>If this server or its encryption key were ever exposed, someone could use your saved council session the way you can &mdash; to view what is held in your ePermits account and manage the permits in it. Changing your ePermits password shuts the session out immediately. Encryption makes that exposure unlikely, using a password that is unique to your council account keeps any fallout contained there, and &mdash; as with any online service &mdash; none of this is an absolute guarantee.</p>
    </details>

    <h2 class="about-h2">Notifications</h2>
    <p>p.stonn tries to tell you, by email and/or push, each time it changes your permit or can&rsquo;t. This is best-effort: messages can be delayed, filtered, or lost, and the service can be down. Treat it as a convenience, not a guarantee &mdash; you remain responsible for your permit and for any fines.</p>

    <h2 class="about-h2">For the City of Stonnington</h2>
    <p>If you work for the council and have questions about this service, please get in touch &mdash; happy to talk. p.stonn acts only with each resident&rsquo;s own login, on their own permit, and only when that resident&rsquo;s schedule needs a change. It signs in the same way the ePermits website does, then uses the council&rsquo;s own permit API to change the vehicle &mdash; and on those API requests it identifies itself as p.stonn, with a link back to this site. It keeps its load light: a single plate change is three requests (read the current vehicle, change it, read back to confirm), fewer than a resident doing the same by hand in a browser; between changes it touches the council only a handful of times a day &mdash; one request roughly every eight hours to keep the session from lapsing, and a permit read twice a day to stay in sync. All told that is on the order of a dozen requests across a whole day for one household, spaced out and backing off if the portal is busy. If the council offers permit scheduling natively, or an official way for residents to delegate access, this app will adopt it or retire.</p>

    <h2 class="about-h2">No promises</h2>
    <p>p.stonn is provided as-is, with no warranty of any kind. It may stop working, make mistakes, or lose data. Use it at your own risk.</p>
  </section>
